sentences.text: Carlo Messina, born in Rome in 1962, has been Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Intesa Sanpaolo since 29 September 2013.

sentences.quote: A graduate of Economics and Business from Luiss University of Rome, he began his career at Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, where he held the position of Manager in charge of the Corporate Finance - Primary Markets and Corporate Finance Department.
sentences.text: A graduate in Economics and Business from Luiss University in Rome, he began his career at Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, where he was manager in charge of the Corporate Finance and Primary Markets department.

sentences.quote: In 1992, he joined Bonifiche Siele Finanziaria (Parent Company of the Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura banking group), where he held the position of Manager in charge of the Planning and Strategic Control Department. From 1996, he was Manager in charge of Planning at Banco Ambrosiano Veneto and, in 2002, he became the Head of the Planning and Control Head Office Department at Banca Intesa.
sentences.text: He later joined Bonifiche Siele Finanziaria in 1992 as head of planning and strategic control, ran planning at Banco Ambrosiano Veneto from 1996, and in 2002 became Head of the Planning and Control Head Office Department at Banca Intesa.

sentences.quote: At Intesa Sanpaolo, in 2007, he was Head of the Value Creation Governance Area, became Chief Financial Officer in 2008, General Manager and Chief Financial Officer in 2012. In 2013, he took on the role of General Manager of the Bank, Head of the Chief Financial Officer Governance Area and Head of the Banca dei Territori Division.
sentences.text: At Intesa Sanpaolo he headed the Value Creation Governance Area in 2007, served as Chief Financial Officer from 2008, became General Manager and CFO in 2012, and added responsibility for the Banca dei Territori Division in 2013 before his appointment as CEO.

mgmt_bio.text: Carlo Messina, born in Rome in 1962, has been Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Intesa Sanpaolo since 29 September 2013. A graduate in Economics and Business from Luiss University in Rome, he began his career at Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, where he was manager in charge of the Corporate Finance and Primary Markets department. He later joined Bonifiche Siele Finanziaria in 1992 as head of planning and strategic control, ran planning at Banco Ambrosiano Veneto from 1996, and in 2002 became Head of the Planning and Control Head Office Department at Banca Intesa. At Intesa Sanpaolo he headed the Value Creation Governance Area in 2007, served as Chief Financial Officer from 2008, became General Manager and CFO in 2012, and added responsibility for the Banca dei Territori Division in 2013 before his appointment as CEO.

sentences.quote: INTESA SANPAOLO IS ABLE TO GENERATE SOLID SUSTAINABLE PROFITABILITY, WITH A NET INCOME OF EUR 5.6 BILLION (+6.5% ON H1 2025). 2026 NET INCOME OUTLOOK UPGRADED TO OVER EUR 10 BILLION.
sentences.text: Intesa Sanpaolo is delivering record profitability, with H1 2026 net income of EUR 5.6bn, up 6.5% year on year, and the 2026 outlook upgraded to over EUR 10bn, alongside 20% ROE and 25% ROTE.

sentences.quote: Intesa Sanpaolo operates an integrated Wealth Management, Protection and Advisory platform, built on fully owned product factories and distribution networks working under full strategic control.
sentences.text: Growth is fee-led through an integrated wealth management, protection and advisory platform with fully owned product factories and distribution networks, supported by customer financial assets above EUR 1.5 trillion.

Shareholder distribution is a core pillar, with around EUR 9.4bn expected to be returned in 2026 via dividends and buybacks and roughly EUR 50bn of capital return over 2025-2029 at a 75% cash payout plus 20% buybacks.

sentences.quote: Annualized Cost of risk was 20 basis points, with a strong increase in coverage and no overlays released.
sentences.text: Capital and asset quality are strong, with a CET1 ratio of 13.1%, a target comfortably above 12.5% and a net NPL ratio of 0.8% with annualized cost of risk at 16 basis points.
Cost discipline adds operating leverage, as first-half operating costs fell 0.7% while operating margin rose 9.1%.
